fields.meta_description: Build freight broker automation that prices emailed quote requests, checks carrier insurance, tracks driver ETAs, and audits carrier invoices.
fields.h1: Build Freight Broker Automation Around Every Load
fields.hero_description: Build freight broker automation that turns shipper emails into quotes and flags late loads before the shipper calls.
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds one app from your prompt for the quote desk and the carrier side, with your own margin and coverage rules.
fields.feature_1:
Quote requests read from shipper emails

The app reads each emailed quote request into a draft quote with the lane and equipment, plus the pickup date. It prices the lane from your past loads and holds thin margins.
fields.feature_2:
Carrier packets checked on arrival

The app collects each carrier's W-9, signed agreement, and insurance certificate. AI reads each coverage amount and expiry date, and a person confirms any field it is unsure of.
fields.feature_3:
Driver check-ins from an email link

Drivers open a check-in link sent by email and enter their location and ETA, with no app to install. Each check-in is saved on the load and moves its pin on the load board.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts that go to the rep on the load

A quote under the margin floor, a carrier short on coverage, or a late ETA reaches the rep who owns that load in Slack or email. Reminders repeat until the rep acts.
fields.feature_5:
Your TMS and accounting kept in sync

Connect your TMS and QuickBooks, or any other tool with an API. Booked loads come in from the TMS and approved carrier bills go out, with each record kept in a database you own.
fields.feature_6:
The brokerage app's code, in your GitHub

Export the full code of the brokerage app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Your developer can review how rates and carrier data are stored, as with any other codebase.

fields.tab_content_1:
Q-2291 falls below its margin floor at $1,800

Rathbone Mills emails Brindlecote Freight for a dry van from Dallas to Memphis at a target rate of $1,800. The app reads it into quote Q-2291 and prices the lane from the last 3 loads, which cost $1,650 on average. That leaves $150 of margin, and any quote under $200 of margin waits for Arvo Ingersoll, the account rep.
fields.tab_content_2:
Pikeview waits with $75,000 of cargo cover

Pikeview Transport sends a W-9, the signed carrier agreement, and an insurance certificate. The app reads $75,000 of cargo coverage on the certificate. Any carrier under the $100,000 minimum stays off the tender list, and Sabela Moraes, the carrier rep, gets a direct message to ask for an updated certificate.
fields.tab_content_3:
The 2:00 PM appointment on L-40872 slips to 3:30 PM

The Northgate Carriers driver on load L-40872 checks in at 11:15 AM from an emailed link with an ETA of 3:30 PM. The receiver's appointment is at 2:00 PM, so the load will arrive 90 minutes late. Any ETA more than 60 minutes past the appointment sends Folarin Lamont, the ops rep, a direct message to call the receiver.
fields.tab_content_4:
Before Bellwood is paid, billing rules on $150 of detention

Bellwood Trucking invoices $2,250 for load L-40915 with the signed proof of delivery. The app reads both and matches the $2,100 linehaul to the rate confirmation. The other $150 is detention. Any charge missing from the rate confirmation waits for Grisette Ottery, the billing lead, before Bellwood is paid.

fields.howto_title: How to Build Freight Broker Automation
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up freight broker automation that handles each load's paperwork and exceptions, tested on past loads first.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pull a month of closed loads
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put a number in every hold rule
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Name an owner for each exception
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Describe the app in one prompt
fields.howto_step_1_des: Export last month's closed loads from your TMS with the lane, shipper, carrier, carrier cost, sell rate, and any accessorials paid. These rows price new quotes and become the test set in step 7. Keep the loads that went wrong.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write each hold rule as one sentence with a number in it, such as a margin floor in dollars or a minimum cargo limit. A rule with no number leaves the rep guessing what counts as low, and the app has nothing to compare against.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick one person for each kind of exception: the account rep for thin quotes, the carrier rep for short coverage, the ops rep for late loads, and the billing lead for extra charges. Each alert goes to that person, never to a shared channel.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Describe your inboxes, the files carriers send, the rules from step 2, and the owners from step 3 in a prompt. Emergent builds the quote intake, the carrier packet checks, the check-in link, the invoice match, and the database behind them.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Connect your TMS and accounting system through their APIs, such as QuickBooks or Xero. Loads booked in the TMS flow into the app, and carrier bills you approve post to accounting. Nobody on the desk types the same load twice.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide when drivers get the check-in email, for example at pickup and again 2 hours before the delivery appointment. Then set the late threshold in minutes and whether a late load also sends the shipper an email from the account rep.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Replay last month before going live
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run the loads from step 1 through the app and compare its holds with what your team did at the time. If it holds a quote your rep sent at a fair margin, adjust that rule, then switch on the live inboxes.

faq_plan.a: Freight broker automation is software that runs the repeat steps of brokering a load without a person keying each one: reading quote requests, checking carrier paperwork, collecting check-ins, and matching carrier invoices. People still decide the exceptions, such as a thin margin or a charge nobody agreed to.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up freight broker automation?
faq_plan.a: Start with a month of closed loads and a written list of hold rules, each with a number and an owner. Describe both in a prompt to Emergent's AI automation builder, which builds the app and its database. Then connect your TMS and replay past loads before the live inboxes go on.

faq_plan.q: Which tasks can AI automation for freight brokers take over?
faq_plan.a: The tasks that arrive as text or documents: shipper quote emails, insurance certificates, proof of delivery, and carrier invoices. AI reads each one into fields, and anything it reads with low confidence goes to a rep to confirm. Pricing calls and carrier choice stay with your people.

faq_plan.q: Can logistics automation send shippers a weekly capacity email?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The app can read next week's lanes where you have carriers lined up and email each shipper only the lanes they ship on, every Monday morning. For a list-based email with sign-ups and unsubscribes, newsletter automation is the closer fit.

faq_plan.q: How do I add carrier onboarding to freight broker automation?
faq_plan.a: Send each new carrier one upload link for the whole packet, and have the app check each file as it lands. The app collects W-9s and keeps payment records ready for 1099 reporting, though it does not file taxes. Add a reminder to the carrier rep 30 days before any certificate expires.

faq_plan.q: Should freight broker automation match carrier invoices to the rate confirmation?
faq_plan.a: Yes, because the rate confirmation is the agreed price for that load. FreightWaves calls it a binding contract between the carrier and the broker. A charge missing from it is a question for billing before anyone pays it.

faq_plan.q: Can freight broker automation post loads that still need a carrier?
faq_plan.a: Yes, to any channel with an API. The app can post each load still uncovered 2 hours after booking to your carrier email list, with the lane and pickup window. Posting the same loads to LinkedIn or X is a job for social media automation.

faq_plan.q: How does freight broker automation handle detention claims?
faq_plan.a: It checks each claim against the driver's check-ins, using the free time and hourly rate from the rate confirmation. Detention is charged when a truck is held beyond the agreed-upon free time for loading or unloading. The app counts the hours between the arrival and departure check-ins. A claim longer than the check-ins show waits for billing.

faq_plan.q: What records should freight broker automation keep for every load?
faq_plan.a: Keep the quote, the rate confirmation, every check-in, the signed proof of delivery, and both invoices on one load record, along with who approved each hold. Emergent builds the app on a database you own, and a dispute months later starts from that single record.

faq_plan.q: How does freight broker automation follow up on unanswered quotes?
faq_plan.a: With a rule on open quotes. If a shipper has not replied 24 hours after the quote went out, the app emails a short reminder with the rate and pickup date. After a second silence, it marks the quote lost for the rep to review. It is the same pattern abandoned cart automation uses for online stores. With no task cap in Emergent, every open quote gets its follow-up.
